correctness.rationale: The prefix Boolean occupancy is an autonomous eight-state continuous-time Markov chain: arrivals set the first bit, and a gate empties its bit and sets the next bit only when carrying a nonempty batch. With r>0 one can clear the prefix without arrivals and build any target occupancy from right to left, proving irreducibility. An independent symbolic solve and polynomial expansion reproduce every displayed stationary mass and Rayleigh quadratic. Each quadratic has positive leading coefficient for r>0, with the same discriminant r^6(r²−16r−16)/[256(1+r)^10]. The all-real Rayleigh criterion therefore gives precisely 0<r≤8+4√5, including equality. Evaluating the three differences at the all-ones point gives strict negative unweighted covariances. Under the positive middle-site tilt the covariance of the endpoints is −Δ_13(t)/F(1,t,1)^2; the denominator is positive and the numerator sign reduces to r²(t²−t)+4(r+1). Its two roots lie in (0,1) above threshold, as stated, and at equality the covariance is zero rather than positive at t=1/2. The prefix is the same marginal in any longer finite stationary ASIP, and specialization of a stable Boolean generating polynomial at 1 preserves stability here because the marginal is nonzero. No low-rate claim for longer chains follows.
residual_risks: The field is a statistical probability tilt, not a change to the dynamics, and the result does not characterize stability for all longer chains below the threshold.

evidence: Reuveni et al. give exact interval-load probabilities; Lauber Bonomo and Reuveni compute the covariance matrix of integer site populations. Borcea–Brändén–Liggett provide the general criterion and field closure.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Knowing interval loads or count covariances is not the same as knowing the all-real Rayleigh inequalities of a three-bit occupancy law. Even an antecedent full stationary PGF would supply the law, not itself the critical sign classification.

Integer-count covariances cannot substitute for covariances of vacancy/nonvacancy indicators; in particular negative ordinary covariances do not establish all-real polynomial inequalities.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The general theory establishes why a positive tilted covariance is an obstruction and how to prove sufficiency. It does not give the particular threshold or prove that one positive field already witnesses the entire unstable range.

originality.rationale: The ASIP model, stationary probability methods, and the multiaffine real-stability criterion are known. The distinct supported result is the exact joint Boolean stability boundary and the exact field-induced endpoint correlation reversal despite strictly negative ordinary covariances. Inspected occupation laws and integer-count covariance results do not state or give this threshold without a fresh Boolean joint-law and Rayleigh sign calculation. No equivalent earlier ASIP statement was substantiated; the founding article is an explicit full-text access risk.
residual_risks: The 2011 ASIP article was not accessible in full, and the precise staircase analogue was not retrieved. Neither limit is negative evidence.
The comparison does not exclude unindexed exact ASIP calculations.

value.rationale: This is a sharp, interpretable boundary in a standard interacting-particle model, not just an isolated sign check. Ordinary pairwise correlations remain negative throughout, but one concrete physical-site reweighting distinguishes all rates above the boundary and quantifies the full detection interval. The three-site obstruction immediately rules out strong Rayleigh for every longer homogeneous prefix above threshold.
residual_risks: There is no characterization of longer lengths below threshold or identification of the field with a dynamical gate change.
